lead.headline: Trump says deportation drive was 'too tough' after midterm rout
lead.dek: In a 60 Minutes interview, the president gave himself an A+ on the border and said he would attack Iran again
body: President Donald Trump said Sunday that his administration's deportation campaign was "too tough" on long-settled immigrants with jobs, his first concession on the policy since Republicans lost both chambers of Congress on Tuesday. He spoke to CBS News' Ross Douthat in a 60 Minutes interview broadcast Sunday night.

Trump said immigration "both helped and hurt" him at the polls and that he earned "an A+ for closing up the border," but that people working at landscaping companies or hotels and paying taxes were removed too. Exit polling cited by CBS found 58% of voters said the immigration actions had gone too far and 63% disapproved of his performance; Trump said the main reason for the losses was that "I was not on the ballot."

He said he would answer "emphatic yes" if asked whether he would strike Iran again, called impeachment calls against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth "Very unfair," and said he would "love to do something on immigration" with Democrats. On Friday, about an hour after the taping, Trump named Stephen Miller, the deportation policy's architect, to replace Susie Wiles as chief of staff.

briefs.headline: Jeffries backs Hegseth impeachment as Blanche warns Democrats
briefs.summary: The incoming speaker told ABC he is "a hard yes" on the Massie resolution expected within days; Attorney General Todd Blanche said probes of Democrats over "threatening" rhetoric are possible.

briefs.headline: Nvidia board opens probe as Huang admits affair to staff
briefs.summary: A committee of independent directors will review the Times report that a Megaspeed executive sought ties to the CEO; the board said it has no reason to believe secrets were compromised. Three House Republicans want Huang to testify Nov. 18.

briefs.headline: Peltola sues Alaska for records on rejected absentee ballots
briefs.summary: The Democrat, 637 votes ahead of Sen. Dan Sullivan, asked Anchorage Superior Court to make the Division of Elections release rejected absentee voters' names and the reasons; ranked-choice tabulation is Nov. 18, certification Nov. 25.

briefs.headline: Deputy chief of staff Walters resigns in first exit under Miller
briefs.summary: Richard Walters, a longtime Susie Wiles ally, told CBS News he resigned Friday; incoming chief of staff Stephen Miller called him "an invaluable member of the White House." It is the first senior exit since Miller was named.

briefs.headline: Rubio sees no breakthrough as Qatar's premier brings Iran offer
briefs.summary: Marco Rubio called Iran's terms "outrageous" and said "I wouldn't say we're at the verge of a breakthrough"; Qatar's Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani meets Trump Monday, and Iran says its two-day offer to reopen Hormuz stands.

briefs.headline: Train rams stopped train near Cairo, killing 7 and injuring 125
briefs.summary: A Giza-to-Fayoum train hit the rear of a stopped Cairo-to-Aswan service at al-Ayyat about 1:30 p.m. Sunday, derailing six carriages, the Health Ministry said; President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi ordered an urgent investigation.

briefs.headline: Krakow gunman dies in hospital as Poland begins two days of mourning
briefs.summary: Police said Monday the suspect in Saturday's square shooting that killed six had died; prosecutors opened a terrorism inquiry Sunday, and Prime Minister Donald Tusk said no one intends to ban Wednesday's Independence March.

briefs.headline: Mexico arrests Jalisco cartel cell leader 'R2' on DEA intelligence
briefs.summary: Marines and federal agents wounded and captured Rafael Alvarez in Zapopan on Sunday and held 19 others; Security Minister Omar Garcia Harfuch tied him to at least 19 killings, including the Uruapan mayor's, and a U.S. extradition request.

briefs.headline: Superintendent briefs lawmakers Monday on school funding
briefs.summary: Michele Blatt and finance officer Uriah Cummings go before the Joint Standing Committee on Education at 2 p.m. as lawmakers weigh replacing the enrollment-based formula.

briefs.headline: Justices rule courts cannot settle Methodist property split
briefs.summary: Justice Charles Trump wrote, with no dissents, that 33 congregations' bid to keep their buildings after leaving the United Methodist Church belongs to church tribunals.

briefs.headline: State certified Boone County data center without announcement
briefs.summary: Commerce approved LM Core's Project Country Roads at the former Hobet mine site Sept. 30 with no announcement, the Gazette-Mail found; filings cite 3,557 acres and 1.4 gigawatts.

briefs.headline: Moundsville-area fire forces shelter order, closes W.Va. 2
briefs.summary: A fire at Sweirkos Enterprises in Washington Lands kept residents indoors until 5:40 p.m. Sunday and closed W.Va. 2; Washington Lands Elementary goes remote Monday.

regional.item: The State Police Cold Case Task Force has taken on Huntington's unsolved 2005 prom-night shooting that killed four, Sen. Mike Woelfel said.
An overturned camper closed westbound I-64 near Nitro for about 90 minutes Sunday afternoon; police said no one was hurt.
Parkersburg City Council votes Tuesday on final reading of a raise for the next mayor, from $90,000 to $125,000, effective in 2029.
Hinton's fire department sold raffle tickets Saturday toward restoring the city's first fire truck, a Seagrave delivered in 1926.

away.item: A Bennington stable's 10-year-old Morgan was unanimous grand champion at the breed's Oklahoma City world show, the Banner said Sunday.

hotspots.item: WVSSAC's schedule released Sunday sends No. 13 Webster County to No. 4 East Hardy at 4 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 14, in the Class A first round.
Pender County's school board is expected to vote Monday on a Topsail Middle renovation now estimated at $50.9M, up from $30M in September.

briefs.headline: Second storm leaves 10,561 Interior customers in the dark
briefs.summary: BC Hydro said 135,000 customers were out at the 1 a.m. Sunday peak and 10,561 in the central Interior, Prince George included, were still dark late morning; the worst damage is east and north of the city.

briefs.headline: Driver dies under fallen tree in Surrey as third storm nears
briefs.summary: Surrey police said a tree and wires fell on two vehicles on Highway 10 at 7:58 p.m. Saturday, killing one driver; Environment Canada expected a third storm Monday with gusts to 90 km/h.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court hears challenge to Ottawa's 2020 firearms ban
briefs.summary: Arguments run Monday and Tuesday on whether cabinet exceeded its authority in banning more than 1,500 models, since expanded past 2,500; Alberta, Saskatchewan and Ontario back the challengers.

briefs.headline: Quebec ex-official charged over 100 false immigration papers
briefs.summary: The anti-corruption agency charged Marilena Ida, a former Immigration Ministry co-ordinator, with breach of trust and forgery; Minister Catherine Gentilcore said she was "deeply shocked." Ida appears in court Dec. 10.

briefs.headline: Ozone hole ranks seventh largest in 48 years, NASA says
briefs.summary: The hole reached its 2026 maximum Sept. 18 as an unusually strong polar vortex spread depletion over a wide area, NASA said; it was not as deep as other large holes on record.

briefs.headline: Cambridge mRNA therapy regrows heart muscle in mice
briefs.summary: A short-lived mRNA switching on two proteins raised blood pumped per beat about 10% in mice after a heart attack, with gains lasting 12 weeks, Cambridge reported in Nature Cardiovascular Research.

briefs.headline: Bergen team names largest known megapode from Flores cave
briefs.summary: A leg bone found in 2009 at Liang Bua, the Homo floresiensis cave, is a new 3.9 kg species 120,000 to 190,000 years old, researchers reported in Alcheringa; it is the first megapode fossil from Wallacea.

briefs.headline: Divers map 1.56 km rose coral colony at Cocos Islands
briefs.summary: Adelaide University's JP Hobbs needed 12 dives to map the Pachyseris colony on the outer reef slope at 14 to 65 metres, Queensland Museum said; genetic tests will show whether it is one organism.

briefs.headline: NYU model flags every PTSD case in 30-patient ER test
briefs.summary: PREVIA, an ensemble of open-source Llama and Mistral models reading trauma narratives, caught all 30 patients who later developed PTSD against 89% for a specialist clinician, NYU Langone reported in Nature Communications.

briefs.headline: Torvalds relays claim AI kernel fixes now outpace reports
briefs.summary: Releasing Linux 7.4 rc2 with "various AI fixes," Linus Torvalds quoted eBPF lead Alexei Starovoitov that fixes in that subsystem now arrive faster than new reports, adding it "sounds lovely if true."

briefs.headline: AI safety center staff now report to White House, AP says
briefs.summary: Two former officials told the AP that staff at the Commerce Department's $10M-a-year CAISSI were asked to report informally to a White House office; the center has had no permanent head since April.

art.caption: A derailed carriage of the Cairo-to-Aswan train tilted up an embankment at al-Ayyat, Giza, on Sunday, with a crowd gathered below.
art.credit: Sketched from an Al Jazeera photograph

kicker: Nicholas-Webster carries no regional line today; a decision on two Nicholas County school closures is due Tuesday.
